title: Use of the Atomic Bomb in WWII
rootClaim: The use of atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki was unjustified and morally indefensible.

branches.text: Mass killing of non-combatants and innocent civilians violates fundamental principles of just war theory and international humanitarian law.

children.text: Civilian populations in Hiroshima and Nagasaki were intentionally targeted to maximize psychological shock and terror.
Radiation sickness and intergenerational genetic defects caused prolonged, indiscriminate human suffering long after the initial blast.
Radiation poisoning affected generations of Hibakusha, resulting in exceptionally high rates of leukemia, severe birth defects, and social ostracization.

branches.text: Japan was already on the verge of total economic collapse and actively seeking terms of surrender, rendering nuclear weapons militarily unnecessary.

children.text: Allied naval blockades and conventional strategic bombing had obliterated Japan's industrial capacity, merchant fleet, and oil reserves.
The Soviet invasion of Manchuria (Operation August Storm) shattered Japanese military hopes of a negotiated peace, serving as the decisive catalyst for surrender.
High Command in Tokyo was far more alarmed by Soviet entry and potential Communist occupation than by atomic strikes on provincial cities.

branches.text: The decision to drop the bombs was heavily driven by geopolitical posturing to intimidate the Soviet Union at the dawn of the Cold War.

children.text: US political leaders expedited the atomic strikes specifically to compel Japanese surrender before Soviet forces could claim major territorial concessions in East Asia.

branches.text: The bombings prevented a full-scale invasion of mainland Japan (Operation Downfall), saving hundreds of thousands of Allied and Japanese lives.

children.text: The fierce, suicidal defense at Okinawa and Iwo Jima demonstrated that a mainland invasion would result in catastrophic casualties on both sides.
Fanatical civilian mobilization under the Ketsu-Go doctrine meant Japanese resistance during an invasion would have led to widespread civilian deaths anyway.
Casualty estimates for Operation Downfall were retroactively inflated by military and political leaders to justify the deployment of atomic weapons to the public.
Total war doctrine had already erased the practical distinction between combatant and non-combatant targets through strategic carpet bombing campaigns.

definitions.description: The Japanese term for the surviving victims of the 1945 atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
The overall Allied plan for the invasion of Japan, which was rendered unnecessary by Japan's surrender.
A framework of ethical criteria determining whether a war is morally justified, emphasizing discrimination between combatants and non-combatants.
The Japanese defense strategy for the home islands aimed at inflicting unbearable casualties on invading Allied forces to negotiate better peace terms.
